# dlaqz4

> Executes a single multishift QZ sweep on a matrix pencil.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlaqz4 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlaqz4';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlaqz4(
    order,
    ilschur, ilq, ilz,
    N,
    ilo, ihi, nshifts,
    nblock_desired,
    SR, strideSR,
    SI, strideSI,
    SS, strideSS,
    A, LDA,
    B, LDB,
    Q, LDQ,
    Z, LDZ,
    QC, LDQC,
    ZC, LDZC,
    WORK
) → integer
```

Executes a single multishift QZ sweep on the matrix pencil `(A, B)`.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout (`'row-major'` or `'column-major'`) |
| `ilschur` | `boolean` | in |  |  | if true, update the full Schur form |
| `ilq` | `boolean` | in |  |  | if true, update the matrix `Q` |
| `ilz` | `boolean` | in |  |  | if true, update the matrix `Z` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | order of the matrices |
| `ilo` | `integer` | in |  |  | (0-based) first index of the active Hessenberg region |
| `ihi` | `integer` | in |  |  | (0-based) last index of the active Hessenberg region |
| `nshifts` | `integer` | in |  |  | desired number of shifts |
| `nblock_desired` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | rejects `nblock_desired < nshifts + 1` | desired size of the computational windows |
| `SR` | `Float64Array` | in |  |  | real parts of the shifts |
| ↳ `strideSR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `SR` |
| `SI` | `Float64Array` | in |  |  | imaginary parts of the shifts |
| ↳ `strideSI` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `SI` |
| `SS` | `Float64Array` | in |  |  | scales of the shifts |
| ↳ `strideSS` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `SS` |
| `A` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N × N` |  | matrix `A` |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  |  | leading dimension of `A` |
| `B` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N × N` |  | matrix `B` |
| ↳ `LDB` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  |  | leading dimension of `B` |
| `Q` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `null × N` |  | matrix `Q` |
| ↳ `LDQ` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  |  | leading dimension of `Q` |
| `Z` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `null × N` |  | matrix `Z` |
| ↳ `LDZ` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  |  | leading dimension of `Z` |
| `QC` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `null × nblock_desired` |  | workspace matrix |
| ↳ `LDQC` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  |  | leading dimension of `QC` |
| `ZC` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `null × nblock_desired` |  | workspace matrix |
| ↳ `LDZC` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  |  | leading dimension of `ZC` |
| `WORK` | `(Float64Array\|null)` | out | `≥ max( 1, N )` |  | workspace of size at least `N * nblockDesired` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `ilschur`: Determines whether or not to update the full Schur form
- `ilq`: Determines whether or not to update the matrix Q
- `ilz`: Determines whether or not to update the matrix Z
- `N`: The order of the matrices A, B, Q, and Z. $N \ge 0$.
- `nshifts`: The desired number of shifts to use
- `nblock_desired`: The desired size of the computational windows
- `SR`: the real parts of the shifts to use.
- `SI`: the imaginary parts of the shifts to use.
- `SS`: the scale of the shifts to use.
- `WORK`: On exit, if $\mathrm{INFO} \ge 0$, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (`0` on success, negative on illegal argument)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `RangeError` ninth argument is invalid (rejected when `nblock_desired < nshifts + 1`)
- `RangeError` `N` must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` `LDA` must be a positive integer
- `RangeError` `LDB` must be a positive integer

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlaqz4.ndarray(
    ilschur, ilq, ilz,
    N,
    ilo, ihi, nshifts,
    nblock_desired,
    SR, strideSR, offsetSR,
    SI, strideSI, offsetSI,
    SS, strideSS, offsetSS,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    B, strideB1, strideB2, offsetB,
    Q, strideQ1, strideQ2, offsetQ,
    Z, strideZ1, strideZ2, offsetZ,
    QC, strideQC1, strideQC2, offsetQC,
    ZC, strideZC1, strideZC2, offsetZC,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → integer
```

Executes a single multishift QZ sweep on the matrix pencil `(A, B)`.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ilschur` | `boolean` | in |  |  | if true, update the full Schur form |
| `ilq` | `boolean` | in |  |  | if true, update the matrix `Q` |
| `ilz` | `boolean` | in |  |  | if true, update the matrix `Z` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | order of the matrices |
| `ilo` | `integer` | in |  |  | (0-based) first index of the active Hessenberg region |

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `nshifts < 2` or `ilo >= ihi`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dlaqz4()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLAQZ4`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dlaqz4.f).
-   The active range is `[ilo, ihi]` using 0-based indices. The pencil `(A, B)` must be in upper Hessenberg / upper triangular form on this range.
-   `nshifts` is rounded down to an even number internally; if the shifts are not yet paired into complex-conjugate pairs, the routine performs a one-pass shuffle to move unpaired real shifts to the end of the active region before sweeping.
-   `QC` and `ZC` are workspace square matrices used to accumulate the local Givens rotations before applying them to the trailing pencil via `dgemm`. They are sized `nblockDesired`-by-`nblockDesired`.
-   `WORK` must hold at least `N * nblockDesired` doubles. Each `dgemm` writes its product into the leading `SHEIGHT * SWIDTH` columns of `WORK`, which is then copied back into the destination block via `dlacpy`.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dlaqz4 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlaqz4';

const N = 6;
const A = new Float64Array( N * N );
const B = new Float64Array( N * N );
const Q = new Float64Array( N * N );
const Z = new Float64Array( N * N );
const QC = new Float64Array( N * N );
const ZC = new Float64Array( N * N );
const WORK = new Float64Array( N * 4 );
const SR = new Float64Array( [ 1.5, 1.5 ] );
const SI = new Float64Array( [ 0.3, -0.3 ] );
const SS = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 1.0 ] );
let i, j;

// Build a small Hessenberg-triangular pencil (A, B) of order N=6, column-major:
for ( j = 1; j <= N; j++ ) {
	for ( i = 1; i <= N; i++ ) {
		if ( i <= j + 1 ) {
			A[ ( i - 1 ) + ( ( j - 1 ) * N ) ] = 1.0 + ( 0.1 * ( i + ( 2 * j ) ) ) + ( 0.03 * i * j );
		}
		if ( i <= j ) {
			B[ ( i - 1 ) + ( ( j - 1 ) * N ) ] = 2.0 + ( 0.2 * ( j - i ) ) + ( 0.05 * j );
		}
	}
}
for ( i = 0; i < N; i++ ) {
	Q[ i + ( i * N ) ] = 1.0;
	Z[ i + ( i * N ) ] = 1.0;
}

// Apply a single 2-shift QZ sweep over the full Schur form:
const info = dlaqz4( 'column-major', true, true, true, N, 0, N - 1, 2, 4, SR, 1, SI, 1, SS, 1, A, N, B, N, Q, N, Z, N, QC, N, ZC, N, WORK );

console.log( 'info = ' + info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( A ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>
